clue.text: Sent down for splashing tie with custard?

indicators.note: splashing tie and custard about churns their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A schoolboy is expelled for flicking custard over his tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splashing' rearranges TIE plus CUSTARD; 'with' only joins. Being rusticated is the old Oxbridge term for being sent away from university for a time.
explanation.definitionFit: To be rusticated is to be suspended from a university, which in British usage is being sent down.

clue.text: Twist that's expedient when short of time

indicators.note: short of the time letter means that letter has been removed

parts.note: a trick is a dodge or expedient

explanation.surface: A turn that serves its purpose when the clock is tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when short of' removes T from TRICK. A rick is a sprain, as of the ankle.
explanation.definitionFit: To rick a joint is to wrench or sprain it.

clue.text: Sensible article, in the main, lacking a conclusion

indicators.note: in shows the article sits inside the shortened word for the main
lacking a conclusion means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the main is a poetic name for the sea
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A level-headed piece about the ocean, unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking a conclusion' drops the final A of the sea word, and 'in' sets the article inside what is left. 'the main' is a poetic name for the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of sound mind is being rational and sensible.

clue.text: Little being allowable on loch, of necessity?

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the loch comes below

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous creature
licit means lawful or allowed
Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A tiny sprite permitted on a Scottish lake, presumably by need.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: something done of necessity is implied rather than stated, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The quality of being implied or understood without being said, which the setter likens to something that must follow.

clue.text: Chevalier dumping me for gold in compound

indicators.note: dumping these letters means they are thrown out of the name

parts.note: Maurice Chevalier was the French singer and actor
taken as written

explanation.surface: The French crooner drops the speaker in favour of a gold mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dumping' takes M and E from the ends of MAURICE; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry auric describes trivalent gold in a compound, as opposed to aurous.

clue.text: Mushrooms, select, as a variety

indicators.note: a variety of the words select and as a is a rearrangement of them

explanation.surface: Picking fungi as one kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' signals an anagram of SELECT plus AS A; 'Mushrooms' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to grow rapidly, as a conflict that escalates.

clue.text: American defenders failing to score salute Italian style

parts.note: the CIA, America's intelligence agency, defends the nation
a side that fails to score has nil, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: US defenders who fail to score wave goodbye like Italians.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian greeting used for both hello and goodbye.

clue.text: Turned a bit insane while away?

indicators.note: turned means the words a bit insane are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone went slightly mad during an absence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' rearranges A BIT INSANE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used of a person not present, as in a trial held in their absence.

clue.text: Too much to take

parts.note: reads as something unbearable, but means an excessive quantity of a medicine to swallow

explanation.surface: Something is more than one can bear.
explanation.definitionFit: An excessive amount of a drug is more than should be swallowed.

clue.text: Lags behind, taxing team in fast and hostile league

annotationWithheld.why: Lags behind, taxing team in fast and hostile league (10) for CONSPIRACY: CONS (lags) + RACY (fast) are clear, but no reading of 'behind, taxing team' gives PI, so the clue as held looks garbled
annotationWithheld.clue: Lags behind, taxing team in fast and hostile league

clue.text: Right time to get in a pet

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: The moment has come to work oneself into a sulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a pet' is an old idiom for being in a temper, so 'pet' here is a fit of anger, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet in this old sense is a fit of peevish anger, a temper.

clue.text: Fled vainly as awful Count finally heads European region

indicators.note: heads tells us that letter comes at the front, before the rest
finally points to the last letter of the word Count

parts.note: fled means ran

indicators.note: awful signals the letters of vainly as are jumbled

explanation.surface: The terrible Count heads off a doomed escape across the region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges VAINLY AS into SYLVANIA. The surface nods to Count Dracula's homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: Transylvania is a historical area of Romania, in Europe.

clue.text: Scathingly ridicule cars being distributed

indicators.note: treating the words ridicule and cars scathingly tears them apart and reorders the letters

explanation.surface: Someone mocks cars harshly as they are handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scathingly' is the anagram signal on RIDICULE plus CARS; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To circularise is to send circulars or leaflets out widely, so distributed fits.

clue.text: Presumably financiers in eastern Montana raised support

indicators.note: in puts the financiers inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: MT is the postal abbreviation for Montana
bankmen is an invented word, hence presumably, for people working in banks

explanation.surface: Bankers in eastern Montana backed something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presumably' admits the bank workers' word is invented; 'in' sets it within the state abbreviation. 'raised' belongs to the definition, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: An embankment is a raised bank of earth or stone that holds up a road or holds back water.

clue.text: Hard-core cast lying 'nudie'

indicators.note: cast means thrown into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dishonest nude film with a hard-core cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges LYING plus NUDIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-core supporters are firm and refuse to give way.

clue.text: One begging hopelessly for change?

parts.note: a street beggar asks for loose change; split differently the answer reads as a hopeless reply, '...', to a plea for alteration

explanation.surface: A down-and-out pleads in vain for a few coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A beggar who lives on alms asks passers-by for spare coins.

clue.text: Cause of rush in lane -drain needing repair

indicators.note: needing repair means the letters of lane and drain are broken and put back differently

explanation.surface: A broken drain in a lane causes a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing repair' rearranges LANE plus DRAIN; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The hormone released under stress gives a surge of energy, a rush.

clue.text: Contrasting points about unity in church office

indicators.note: the pair of compass points goes around, so about tells us they enclose the other piece

parts.note: north and south, N and S, are opposite compass points
unity is the number one

explanation.surface: Opposing views on unity within a church department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ONE between N and S. Nones is the monastic prayer service said at the ninth hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Nones is one of the canonical hours, a daily prayer service in monastic worship.

clue.text: Arrange decapitation for abuse?

indicators.note: cutting off the head of the word for abuse removes its opening letter

parts.note: to malign is to abuse verbally, to slander

explanation.surface: Someone orders a beheading as punishment for insults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitation' drops the first letter M from MALIGN; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To line things up in order is to arrange them in a row.

clue.text: Change for girly nest?

indicators.note: changing the words girly nest rearranges their letters

explanation.surface: A young woman's bedroom gets a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges GIRLY NEST, and the whole clue describes what a makeover of a girl's room is.
explanation.definitionFit: A redo of style, as in giving a girl's room a new look, is a makeover.

clue.text: Khaki on Slavs surrendering these?

indicators.note: the letters of khaki on Slavs give themselves up and fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Soldiers in khaki hand over their rifles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrendering' rearranges KHAKI ON SLAVS; the whole clue pictures uniformed Slavic soldiers giving up their weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: The AK-47 assault rifle of Soviet design, the weapon such Slav soldiers would hand over.

clue.text: Carefully ordered last of plonk with almost no effect

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter
almost means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: empty means without effect, as in an empty threat

explanation.surface: The end of the cheap wine had almost no effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of the word for no effect. Plonk is British slang for cheap wine; 'last of' takes its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Kempt means neat and well groomed, tidily arranged.

clue.text: One gets cross at reversing manoeuvre

indicators.note: reversing means the word at is read backwards

parts.note: X is a cross shape
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone gets angry at a reversing move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns AT into TA. 'manoeuvre' is a verb: aircraft taxi along the runway.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft taxi when they move slowly along the ground under their own power.

clue.text: Dutch defence held together by muddy keeper

indicators.note: the letters are held across the join of the words muddy keeper

explanation.surface: A sea wall in the Netherlands is maintained by a dirty warden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held together by' signals letters running across 'muddy keeper'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyke is a sea wall, famously used in the Netherlands to keep the sea out.

clue.text: Long story from city about private investigator

indicators.note: the city's letters go about the detective, enclosing that piece

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A tale from town about a detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the City of London postcode around the detective. EC is the London postcode district for the City.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a lengthy narrative poem or saga.

clue.text: Many retail products providing nourishment

indicators.note: products here means things made out of the words many and retail, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Lots of shop goods are nutritious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'products' signals an anagram of MANY plus RETAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimentary means relating to food and nutrition, so it describes something that feeds.

clue.text: One got back loose habit

indicators.note: back tells us the word got is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: one is A, as in a single item

explanation.surface: Someone has relapsed into a careless routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reads the word got backwards, and one follows. 'habit' means a garment here, not a custom.
explanation.definitionFit: The loose robe worn by Roman citizens is a flowing garment, which is what habit means here.

clue.text: One son comprehending Italian: early sign of infant resourcefulness

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: comprehending means including within, so the native son encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a native son is someone born in a place
IT is short for Italian, as in vermouth

indicators.note: the early sign of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A lad who understands Italian shows early enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehending' sets the Italian abbreviation plus the first letter of 'infant' ('early sign of') inside the word for a son born locally, all after the numeral for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Initiative is the drive to act without being told, i.e. enterprise.
